followUps.title: Decide: bound message and label keys before the P0 freeze (ADR-0005)
followUps.body:
`AuditValidationErrorSchema.key` and `params.labelKey` (`packages/core/src/contracts/audit.ts`) and config `Key` (`packages/core/src/config/schema-fields.ts`) are unbounded `z.string().min(1)`. Tightening after the P0 freeze is a breaking audit change.

Options:
1. Bound message and label keys with one shared pattern in `contracts/primitives.ts`, used by config and audit together (test first).
2. Add an ADR-0005 line recording that they stay unbounded (server-generated keys, never user text).

**Done when:** the developer has chosen, and the choice is merged before the P0 gate.

**Source:** PR #38 wave-review minor M3 (carry W4R-M3).

followUps.title: Sensitive paths: list nested biome.json files and .gitignore
followUps.body:
Biome honours nested `biome.json` files (`root: false`) and `vcs.useIgnoreFile: true` skips files matched by `.gitignore`. A PR can add `packages/core/biome.json` or a `.gitignore` line and switch off lint, including the core purity rule, without a sensitive-review artifact.

Fixed in PR #76 (ADR-0007 tiers): replace `biome.json` with `**/biome.json` and add `.gitignore` in `.github/sensitive-paths` (or set `useIgnoreFile: false` and rely on `files.includes`), mirror in CLAUDE.md, and extend the shipped-glob test in `scripts/ci/sensitive-review.test.ts`. PR #76 lists both in `[gate]` and closes this issue.

**Source:** PR #38 wave-review residual RR-M1.

followUps.title: GET /api/v1/config returns only the ClientSiteConfig allowlist
followUps.body:
The route handler must return `toClientSiteConfig(resolved, configHash)`, never the server `SiteConfig`, with a test that `auth`, `retention`, `extends` and `Source.kind`, `server`, `maxConcurrent` are absent from the response.

**Source:** W2 Task 9 carry forward (ledger).

followUps.title: getLocale handler returns 400 validationFailed for a malformed locale
followUps.body:

**Source:** Ruling W3-5, PR #35.

followUps.title: Confirm Better Auth user ids fit BoundedIdSchema
followUps.body:
Audit `actor.id` and credential user ids use `BoundedIdSchema` (`/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/`, ADR-0005). If Better Auth issues ids outside that pattern, every audit write fails closed. Configure or verify the id generator, with a test that a created user's id parses.

**Source:** W1 xhigh review, Track A note (Ruling P-1).

followUps.body:

followUps.title: Threat model: sensitive-review cannot stop a PR editing its own checker
followUps.body:
`sensitive-review` runs on `pull_request`, so a PR can change `ci.yml`, `scripts/ci/sensitive-review.ts` or the lockfile's gate tools and pass without an artifact. Spec 9.1 accepts this (the check proves a review was recorded, and the edit is visible in the diff). Record it in a threat-model doc, and optionally run the base branch's copy of the checker.

**Source:** PR #38 wave-review answer 2.

followUps.title: Core purity lint also catches IO globals
followUps.body:
The Biome override forbids IO imports in `packages/core/src`, but not IO globals that need no import: `fetch`, `process.env`, `WebSocket`, `XMLHttpRequest`. Add a restricted-globals rule for non-test core files, with a probe showing it fires.

**Source:** W4 Task 22 critic minor M3.

followUps.title: Embedded login: validate the host email claim before it reaches audit
followUps.body:
`AuditActor.email` is `z.email().max(254).nullable()`, which rejects host-issued addresses such as `user@cadhost`, IP literals and non-ASCII domains. At `POST /api/v1/auth/embedded`, check the host JWT email claim with `AuditActorSchema.shape.email` and store `null` (or reject the login) when it fails, with a test. Otherwise every audit write, and so every submit (spec 5.2), fails for that principal.

**Source:** PR #38 wave-review minor M2 (carry W4R-M2).

followUps.title: Duplicate response-mapping check uses the canonical when condition
followUps.body:
`checkLimits` keys duplicate response mappings on whether `when` is present, not on the condition itself, so mutually exclusive mappings raise a spurious `duplicateMapping`. Once condition canonicalisation lands, key on the canonical `when`, with a test that distinct conditions pass.

**Source:** W3 Task 13 ruling and carry forward.

followUps.title: Decide: recalibrate review rules before W5 (sdd-task and wave-review by tier)
followUps.body:
ADR-0007 tiered the CI sensitive-review check; our own agent review rules are not tiered yet. PR #76 cost three xhigh reviews (about 1.4M tokens, over 2 hours); W4 cost 74 agents.

Questions to settle before W5:
- `sdd-task`: `sensitive: true` runs Opus medium implementer, fixer, critic, ruler and re-reviewer for every sensitive task. Should gate-tier tasks use ordinary tiers plus the Opus critic, keeping the full set for critical-tier tasks?
- Per-task critic when `wave-review` follows: redundant for gate-tier tasks?
- `wave-review` default effort should follow the PR's highest tier automatically (critical xhigh, gate high), not a manual role override.
- `.claude/workflows/**` and the CLAUDE.md roles table decide how much review everything gets but are in no tier. Gate tier?
- Scope freeze: a PR's sensitive scope is fixed before its review starts; later work goes in the next PR.
- Retro: per role across W1 to W4, which findings were real (spec reviewer, quality reviewer, critic, ruler, checker, re-reviewer).

**Source:** developer, 09-26-26 (after PR #76).

followUps.title: Decide: CI pipeline design before the ruleset (ADR, before W6 Tasks 26 and 28)
followUps.body:
Before the ruleset makes `ci` and `sensitive-review` required (Task 28) and CI grows (Task 26 web build and expo export; Track A P1 image, boot smoke, Playwright, publish), settle the pipeline design so CI never becomes a merge blocker the way the review workflows did on PR #76 (developer, 09-26-26).

- [ ] One stable required check: heavy work in separate jobs, a final `ci` job aggregates them, so new steps never touch the ruleset.
- [ ] Path-scoped jobs: web build, expo export, image and Playwright run only when their paths change (extends the docs-only fast path).
- [ ] Fast fail first: lint and typecheck ahead of parallel heavy jobs; `timeout-minutes` on every job; PR CI budget under 10 minutes.
- [ ] Flake policy: Playwright one retry with trace; quarantine label plus issue; no silent retry loops.
- [ ] External services (oasdiff image, dependency review, pipx zizmor): pinned and cached; an outage fails with a clear message, not a code failure.
- [ ] Break glass: spec 9.1's empty bypass list plus a broken CI deadlocks a CI fix. Who may lift the ruleset (repo admin), when, and how it is logged.
- [ ] Merge style: squash with linear history (spec 9.1) or merge commits for wave PRs, recorded in an ADR.
- [ ] CI duration per PR recorded next to agent metrics.

**Source:** developer, 09-26-26.

followUps.title: Track B P1 plan: align with the P0 tokens, platform and shell (W5 phase critic)
followUps.body:
The W5 phase Opus critic (PR #83) found that the Track B P1 plan (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-25-track-b-p1.md`) contradicts what P0 shipped. Amend the plan before Track B P1 starts:

- [ ] F1 (important): Tasks 1 and 14 still create `packages/client/src/platform.ts` with another shape (`Signal.get`, `WritableSignal`, non-null `tokenStore`, no `clear()`, a `visibility` field; plan lines ~150, 3058, 3114-3116, 5461, 5601). Lead ruling R1: Modify, and use the P0 names (`PlatformSignal.current`, `visible`, nullable `tokenStore`).
- [ ] F4 (important): `styles.css` (plan ~4716-4795) uses variables P0 never emits (`--focus-ring`, `--type-*`, `--space-*`, `--field-required`, `--radius-control`, `--motion-*`), so the focus outline is invalid and no ring shows (spec 6.4). Use the `--qm-` names from `cssVarName` (now including `--qm-focus-ring-width`, `--qm-focus-ring-offset`, `--qm-border-width`, `--qm-color-accent`), drop the literal `48px` (`--qm-target-min`), dedupe `body` and `:focus-visible` with `apps/web/src/shell.css`, and test that no unknown variable is used.
- [ ] F5: Task 12 test expects `:root[data-theme="day"] {`; P0 emits day on bare `:root`.
- [ ] F6: Task 11 quotes stale ratios; `it.each(COLOR_TOKENS)` gets an object (use `Object.keys`).
- [ ] F7: the built entry script has no nonce; under `'strict-dynamic'` the app will not boot unless the API injects one. Use Vite `html.cspNonce` with a placeholder the API replaces, and an e2e check for zero CSP violations (Task 27 dependency).
- [ ] F8: set `document.title` and `<html lang>` from the active locale (NFR-001).
- [ ] F9: reuse P0 `VisuallyHidden` instead of a new `.qm-visually-hidden` class; add `clipPath: "inset(50%)"`.
- [ ] F10: the focus ring colour equals some severity fills; keep offset rings on filled controls and draw badge edges with `color.border`.
- [ ] Shell CSS tests read CSS from disk: a Vite `?raw` CSS import is `""` under Vitest (found in PR #83).

**Source:** W5 phase critic, `.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-25-p0-contracts/w5-phase-critic.md` (Windows ledger), PR #83.

followUps.title: Review cost: split small fixes by tier, board data out of gate, light review for small gate PRs (ADR-0007 amendment, W6)
followUps.body:
Review cost for small gate-tier PRs is out of proportion: #91 (a ReDoS fix plus two small gate edits) pays a full `wave-review` (4 to 5 Opus-high agents, about 0.5M tokens) because `package.json` and `scripts/ops/` are `[gate]` (ADR-0007). Decided by the developer 09-26-26; lands in the W6 PR as an ADR-0007 amendment.

- [ ] **Split small fixes by tier.** An ordinary fix goes in its own PR (CI only). Gate-tier chores ride the next wave PR, which pays for a review anyway. Record it in CLAUDE.md "Controller rules".
- [ ] **Board data out of the gate path.** Move issue numbers, titles, bodies and follow-up data from `scripts/ops/gh-setup-project.mjs` to a data file outside `[gate]` (for example `docs/board/board-data.json`, schema-checked by a test). The script that writes to GitHub stays in `scripts/ops/` (gate). Recording numbers or adding a follow-up becomes an ordinary change.
- [ ] **Light review mode for small gate PRs.** Qualifies: highest tier `[gate]` (never `[critical]`), at most about 50 changed lines in gate paths. One Opus 5.5 agent at effort `medium`, no ruler and no fix pass; findings are fixed inline and the review re-runs; the artifact is written only on approve, front matter `effort: "medium"` plus a light-mode marker. `scripts/ci/sensitive-review.ts` accepts medium only for gate paths and only when it counts the gate-path diff under the limit itself (fails closed on a mislabelled PR). `[critical]` keeps xhigh. Add the mode to `.claude/workflows/wave-review.js` with harness scenarios.
- [ ] ADR-0007 amended (or a superseding ADR); `.claude/workflows/README.md` and CLAUDE.md name the light mode.

Why not Sonnet: gate paths are where a tiny edit switches a check off, and the Opus critic or wave-review caught every fail-open gate the Sonnet reviewers passed (W4: 9 of 9; W5: the lockfile-guard bypass). Changing `sensitive-review.ts` is itself `[critical]`, so the W6 PR takes the xhigh review.

**Source:** developer discussion 09-26-26 after PR #91.

Decide a client receipt policy (drop unknown types, strip unknown keys) or bump `MIN_CLIENT_VERSION` per additive change; record it through master plan 8. (moved to #511)

followUps.title: Decide: can a site default to auto theme (SiteConfig.theme.defaultMode "auto")
followUps.body:
Raised by the Opus critic on Track B P1 Tasks 11 to 13 (wave B3, `resolveThemeMode` in `packages/tokens/src/theme-mode.ts`).

## Current behaviour (spec 6.5, as implemented)

`SiteConfig.theme` is `{ defaultMode: "day" | "night" | "redShift" (default "day"), auto: "off" | "os" | "time" (default "off") }` (`packages/core/src/config/schema.ts:134-135`). `resolveThemeMode` follows 6.5 literally:

- an explicit user preference wins;
- with no site theme loaded (login, all of P1) the OS scheme decides;
- with a site theme, an **unset** preference takes `defaultMode`;
- `theme.auto` applies **only** when the user has explicitly chosen "auto".

So a site that sets `auto: "time"` or `"os"` has no effect on users who never touched the theme picker: they get `defaultMode`, which cannot be `"auto"`.

## Use case

Mobile units working nights: an agency wants every device to follow time of day (or the OS dark setting) out of the box, without each officer opening the theme picker. Today the site can only pick one fixed default mode.

## Decision needed

Can a site default to auto, e.g. `defaultMode: "auto"` (or an equivalent flag), so an unset preference follows `theme.auto`?

A yes is a config contract change under master plan 8: widen the `SiteConfig.theme` schema (and `ClientSiteConfig`), check whether it needs a `CONFIG_SCHEMA_VERSION` bump with a `migrateConfig` step (it is additive, but the check is required), regenerate `site-config.schema.json`, and update `resolveThemeMode` and its tests. This has to land before Track B P2 wires site theme selection from `GET /api/v1/config`. A no keeps today's behaviour and should be recorded in spec 6.5.

IDs: UX-002, UX-011, BR-001 (design spec 6.5).

followUps.title: sensitive-review: files a main merge brings in after reviewedSha count as late
followUps.body:
Found on B5 (#202), checker session 09-28-26. Tier: critical (`scripts/ci/sensitive-review.ts`).

**Problem**
`sensitive-review` flags as "changed after reviewedSha" every critical or gate file in `git diff --name-only <reviewedSha> <head>` (the `nameDiff` call near the `merge-base --is-ancestor` check, then the `late` filter in `evaluateSensitiveReview`). The list is not intersected with the PR's own changed files (`base...head`). So merging `origin/main` into a wave branch after its review makes every sensitive file that main changed count as late, although the PR does not change them. B5 had to re-run wave-review at the merge head (8ebd5d3) to pass.

Workaround until fixed: merge main before wave-review; if main is merged after the review, re-run the review on the merge head.

**Fix**
- [ ] Intersect the late list with the PR's changed files (`base...head`): late = reviewed-tier files changed in `reviewedSha..head` that are also in `changedFiles`.
- [ ] Tests: (1) a main merge after review that brings only main-side sensitive files passes; (2) a PR-touched sensitive file changed after review still fails; (3) a main merge that changes a sensitive file the PR also touches still fails.
- [ ] README "Review tiers" / wave-review notes: drop the "re-review after a main merge" workaround once merged.

Safety: a file outside the PR's diff is not changed by the PR, so dropping it opens no bypass; any PR-touched sensitive file changed after review stays late.

Delivery: own critical PR (not riding a wave PR, so the loosened check is not judging the PR that loosens it; see #70). Implementer Opus 5.5 medium; critical wave-review, fast path if the PR stays within 50 changed lines.

followUps.title: sdd workflows: read head and precondition shas from git, never from agent output
followUps.body:
Found in the A4b sdd-wave run (09-28-26), Task 21. Tier: ordinary (`.claude/workflows/**`).

**What happened.** The T21 round-1 fixer returned `head: 2e31c7761aecdcf5d0f0a1e0a3f9e1a5f6c5e6a1`. That is not a git object: the real commit is `2e31c77c6d9b971f6afc69a7ff4a714fb5315268`, and only the 7-character prefix matches. `sdd-task` used the agent's value as `expectedHead` for gate-r1, so the gate's precondition failed on a clean, correct branch. A controller answer naming the real sha was then refused by the gate agent, which treated it as untrusted task text. The task could not finish inside the run. The controller ran the gate by hand (`pnpm verify`, `pnpm audit --prod`).

**Fix.**
- [ ] Every head and precondition value that `sdd-task.js`, `sdd-wave.js` and `wave-review.js` compare or pass on (`expectedHead`, `reviewHead`, `head`, `base` between tasks, `reviewedSha`) must come from git, never from an agent's JSON. Either resolve and verify with `git rev-parse` in a dedicated step, or have the agent echo raw `git rev-parse HEAD` stdout that the script verifies as a 40-hex sha that exists (`git cat-file -e`) before use.
- [ ] Reject an agent-reported sha that fails that check (log it, then re-read with git) instead of propagating it.
- [ ] A test in `scripts/sdd/workflow-harness.mjs` (or its tests): a fixer that returns a fabricated sha with the correct prefix leads to the real head being used, not a precondition stop.

- [ ] Handle both events in `main.ts`: write one fatal JSON line (error name and a redacted message, never a stack, secret, token or query value), drain or close the server and the DB if possible, and exit non-zero.

followUps.title: WS upgrade: rate limit per IP and no DB lookup before the Origin check
followUps.body:
From the A4b wave-review (`docs/reviews/feat-a-p1-wave-4b.md`, PR #223), a declined-to-judge item. Checker ruling 09-28-26. Tier: gate (`packages/api/src/ws/**`). Priority: Medium.

The WebSocket upgrade on `/api/v1/ws` (`packages/api/src/ws/server.ts`) has no rate limit. Every upgrade, authenticated or not, runs `identity.resolve`, which costs a DB round trip before the Origin check rejects it. An unauthenticated client can therefore drive DB load with a stream of upgrades.

- [ ] Rate-limit upgrades per client IP (reuse `RateLimiter` and `clientIp()`, with a limit stated in the PR and the spec reference), answering 429 before any `identity.resolve`.
- [ ] Reject a disallowed Origin before `identity.resolve`, where that doesn't break the Origin-less bearer path, so a cross-origin upgrade costs no DB lookup.
- [ ] Tests: upgrades over the limit get 429 without calling `identity.resolve` (spy on it); a disallowed Origin never calls `identity.resolve`; a signed-bearer upgrade with no Origin still works.

followUps.title: ci: docs-only push to main skips the image, publish fails and no sha image exists (blocks M0 exit promote)
followUps.body:
**Blocks M0 exit promote.**

From the wave 5 review (`docs/reviews/feat-a-p1-wave-5.md`, PR #229). Tier: gate (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `scripts/ci/ci-workflow.test.ts`).

## Problem

On a docs-only push to `main`, the `image` job is skipped (docs_only gate), so it uploads no `querymodule-image` artifact. `publish` then fails at `download-artifact`: `ci` shows red on `main` and no `ghcr.io/birchdesignlab/querymodule:sha-<sha>` image exists for that commit.

`promote.yml` with `milestone: m0` needs, at the same sha: a successful `ci` run on `main`, `docs/releases/m0.md`, and the `sha-<sha>` image. The M0 exit PR is docs-only (release notes), so the m0 promote cannot pass. Skipping `publish` when `image` is skipped makes `ci` green but still leaves no image at that sha.

## Fix (decided)

Build the image on every push to `main`: the `image` job's docs_only gate applies to pull requests only, so every commit on `main` gets a smoke-tested `sha-<sha>` image and `promote` keeps its invariant (the promoted sha is exactly the image that was built and smoke-tested at that sha). Rejected alternative: promote resolving the image of the nearest ancestor with one, which would promote bytes not built from the named sha and weaken the sha/image equality that rollback relies on.

- [ ] `image` job: `if:` runs on `push` to `main` regardless of docs_only; unchanged for pull requests.
- [ ] `ci-workflow.test.ts`: tests first for both cases (PR docs-only skips `image`; push to main never skips it; `publish` always finds the artifact on main).
- [ ] actionlint and zizmor clean.

Goes in one gate PR with the wave 5 minors issue, after #229 merges and before the M0 exit PR, with its own wave-review (gate Opus 5.5 medium).

followUps.title: Web: a failed sign-out looks like success and leaves the server session valid (SEC-006, spec 5.6, 6.7)
followUps.body:
From the Step 27.7 critic, wave B9 (finding K1, Important). Needs a design decision, and touches packages/client, so it is out of the B9 PR.

**Problem**
- `packages/client/src/auth/auth-api.ts:78-84`: `signOut` swallows network errors and ignores a non-2xx response.
- `packages/client/src/session/session-controller.ts:54-61`: `finally adopt(null)` wipes local state anyway.
- Scenario: on a shared console, Sign out while POST `/api/v1/auth/sign-out` fails (network drop or 5xx). The UI shows the sign-in page, but the session cookie is still valid on the server. The next person reloads, bootstrap calls `getSession`, and they are signed in as the previous user.
- `apps/web/src/home/HomePage.tsx:20-29`: its `catch` (the sign-out error text) can never run with the real controller. If it did run, `adopt(null)` would already have unmounted HomePage.
- `apps/web/src/home/HomePage.test.tsx`: the test passes only because it stubs `session.signOut` to reject, which no real code path does.

**Decision needed**
Should the client wipe locally when the server sign-out fails, and where should the error render (probably the sign-in page, since that is where the user lands)?

**Suggested fix**
- `authApi.signOut` throws on a network error or `!response.ok`.
- The controller keeps the local wipe, then rethrows.
- The sign-in page shows a one-shot "server sign-out failed, retry" message.
- Replace the HomePage test with one where MSW fails `/sign-out`. About 25 to 35 lines.

IDs: SEC-006; spec 5.6 (logout ends the server session), 6.7 (logout resets).

followUps.title: Web: after a failed sign-out, a reload silently signs the previous user back in (SEC-006, spec 5.6, 6.7)
followUps.body:
From the wave B10 UI critic (finding W1, Important). The fix for #235 reports a failed server sign-out, but the flag is in memory only. Needs a design decision.

**Scenario**
- A sign-out fails (503 or network). The device is wiped, but the httpOnly `__Host-` cookie and the server session are still valid.
- The user sees the notice "retry before you leave this device".
- The user closes the tab or reloads, or the next person on a shared MDT reloads. `signOutFailed` (`packages/client/src/auth/auth-store.ts`) is gone.
- `bootstrap()` calls `getSession()`, which succeeds, and adopts the previous user with no notice.

**Options**
- **(a)** Keep the flag in sessionStorage (it is not regulated data) through a `ClientPlatform` storage seam. At boot, when it is set, run `retrySignOut()` before `getSession()`, and adopt nothing if that retry fails. About 15 lines in `session-controller.ts`, plus the seam in `packages/client` platform files.
- **(b)** Record that the developer accepts the risk for the prototype, with the 30-minute idle sweep as the backstop.

IDs: SEC-006; spec 5.6, 6.7.

followUps.title: Web: the update-required gate offers no way to sign out (NFR-001, SEC-006, spec 5.1)
followUps.body:
From the wave B10 UI critic (finding W2, Important). Needs a design decision: should the hard gate from #236 offer sign-out?

**Scenario**
- `MIN_CLIENT_VERSION` is raised mid-shift and a signed-in user reloads.
- The gate (`apps/web/src/app/UpdateRequiredPage.tsx`, `RequireAuth.tsx`) replaces every protected route, including Home, which holds the only Sign out button.
- `/login` redirects a signed-in user to `/`, which is the gate again.
- The user cannot end the session; it lives until the 30-minute idle sweep. On a shared console that matters.

The spec and the #236 ruling neither require nor forbid a way out.

**Suggested fix**
A Sign out button on the gate, using the same `session.signOut().catch(); navigate("/login")` pattern as Home (with the #235 failure notice), plus one Root test. About 15 lines, all in apps/web.

IDs: NFR-001, SEC-006; spec 5.1, 5.6.

followUps.title: Sign-out answers 200 even when the server session row is not deleted (SEC-006, spec 5.6)
followUps.body:
From the wave B11 UI critic (PR for #241/#242), a server-side finding outside Track B's lane. Tier: gate (`packages/api/src/auth/**`). Checker ruling 09-28-26: M1 P2, Track A.

POST `/api/v1/auth/sign-out` (Better Auth) answers 200 even when deleting the session row fails. The client (#235, #241) treats 200 as "server session ended", so a DB failure during sign-out leaves a valid session cookie behind on a shared console with no signal to the user.

- [ ] Audit: `logout` is recorded only when the session row is actually gone (check the existing `logout` audit write order).
- [ ] Tests: a sign-out whose session delete fails answers non-2xx and the session still resolves as live afterwards (so the client retry is meaningful); a normal sign-out still answers 200 and the session no longer resolves.

IDs: SEC-006; spec 5.6.

followUps.title: Logout audit row lost when the audit write fails after Better Auth deletes the session (SEC-010)
followUps.body:
Better Auth deletes the session row before the `logout` audit transaction runs. If that audit write fails, the session is gone with no `logout` row, and a retry cannot write one because no session remains to sign out. Pre-dates #246 and is outside its scope.

- [ ] Decide the order: write the `logout` audit row (or a pending marker) before or atomically with the session delete, fail closed if the audit write fails.
- [ ] Test: audit write failure during sign-out leaves either both (session + no audit) intact or both done; never a deleted session with no `logout` row.

Tier: gate (auth) with audit implications; if the fix touches `packages/api/src/audit/**` it is critical.

**Source:** A0 wave-review follow-up, checker ruling 09-28-26.

followUps.title: Terminal core hardening: parser edge cases, shared helpers, stronger A5 and leak tests (FR-050 to FR-056)
followUps.body:
From wave B2 (PR for #257 to #260): wave-review minors C-M1 to C-M3 plus triaged task-review minors. Tier: critical (`packages/core/src/terminal/**`), own critical PR. Does not block M1 P3.

**Behaviour**
- [ ] A blank token after a named token raises `positionalAfterNamed` at a position the user never typed (`VEH.ZZ-0001.plateType=PC..vin=X` reports position 3) (C-M1).
- [ ] `tooManyPositions` with interior empties reports `{expected:4, got:4}` for `VEH..A.B.C.D`: count every positional token, or reword the spec 4.4 row (C-M2; see the spec 4.4 decisions issue).
- [ ] `formatCommand` counts a preset key as shown even when the draft value differs (`PROF` with `propertyType: BOAT` gives `unshownCount` 0; a merge then overwrites `BOAT`).
- [ ] A preset on a hidden field raises `valueForHiddenField` with no position, for a value the user never typed.
- [ ] `fieldOf`, `isRest`, `readsAsNamed` exist in four copies (`tokenize.ts`, `format.ts`, `parse.ts`/`draft.ts`, `__fixtures__/arbitraries.ts`): one shared helper.
- [ ] `isTrailingEmpty` re-splits the rest once per blank token (O(n²)).
- [ ] Import style: `tokenize.ts` uses extensionless deep imports; `rules/*` uses `.js` and the barrel.

**Tests**
- [ ] Missing edge cases: rest position after a named token; named token with empty value; same named key twice; delimiter-only rest; `valueForHiddenField` on a hidden positioned field; date whose `outputFormat` contains the delimiter.
- [ ] Trailing-empty tests compare `t(a)` with `t(b)` only: also assert the literal result.
- [ ] Leak check (`parse.test.ts`) matches exact, case-sensitive whole tokens only: also catch upper-cased, canonicalised (`26` to `2026`, ISO dates) and substring echoes.
- [ ] Draft round-trip helper passes vacuously when `selectCommand` returns undefined; covers PRO only (add VEH, PER).
- [ ] A5: presets path never runs (shipped sites have none; add an inline config); `canonDraft` drops errors so invalid-on-both-sides compares equal; drafts use ISO dates only, never typed input formats; pin failing counterexamples as fixed cases; idempotence title lacks `[A5]`; `unshownCount` property repeats `formatCommand` logic.
- [ ] `enabledCodes` compiles at `now=0` while the round trip runs at the test date: take `now` as a parameter (C-M3).

**Source:** B2 wave-review artifact `docs/reviews/feat-b-p2-wave-2.md` (reviewed 80adeb6) and task reviews; checker ruling 09-28-26.

followUps.title: Admin UI: console with visual site-config builder for implementers (new scope, design pass)
followUps.body:
Developer direction 09-29-26, after the first live look at the P2 build: forms must be reactive, interactable and configurable from an admin UI; implementers need a visual JSON builder in admin for the site config (fields, rules, picklists, defaults, sources, terminal commands; later M2 response mapping and keywords).

Today BR-001 ("common site customizations through configuration, without code changes") is met by JSON site config files, `config:validate` and a deploy; FR-060 names implementers as the ones who configure. No milestone plans a config editor, and spec 5.8 loads config from files at startup with a `configHash`. This is new scope.

Design pass (Opus 5.5 high, one session) to decide, before any build:
- [ ] Storage: config stays files (builder writes a validated file plus reload) vs a versioned config store in the DB; how `configHash`, the 409 on stale config, and `configLoaded` audit behave on a live change.
- [ ] Editor scope and UX: visual builder over the `SiteConfig` schema (field list, rule conditions, picklists, commands), live preview of the query panel, `validateSiteConfig` diagnostics inline, draft vs publish, rollback.
- [ ] Roles and audit: admin-only (or an `implementer` role), every publish audited, diff shown.
- [ ] Placement in the roadmap: late M2 beside configurable responses (FR-060, UX-010, UX-012), or its own phase; effect on M3 and M4.
- [ ] ADR and spec changes.

P3 (M1) plans are asked to avoid choices that block a later config store or editor.

followUps.body:
The `oasdiff breaking` step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (step 7) is skipped entirely on any PR labelled `api-breaking`. So exactly the PRs that change the API contract get no tool-confirmed diff.

Seen on #611 (M2 P1 AW1): the label was set at open, the step never ran, and the expected breaking changes (`skippedReason` removed from three never-served read routes) plus "no change to the 202" were confirmed only by hand mapping and the review's expectation. followUps.body:
`verifyHead` in `.claude/workflows/sdd-task.js` (#222) accepts only a bare 40-hex `revParse` and an exact `EXISTS <sha>` `catFile`. On 10-13-26 (Track B BW2, run wf_b6cc4809-12d) the Haiku role returned a valid, existing sha but wrapped (JSON text instead of the bare stdout), the strict check rejected it, and the whole `sdd-wave` stopped at `precondition:verifyHead` before Task 5. Recovery cost a session handover and a manual relaunch.

**Fix:** keep the guarantee (the script only uses a sha that git confirmed exists) but parse leniently: take the single 40-hex match from `revParse` (reject zero or several), and require `catFile` to contain `EXISTS <that sha>`. Add tests for bare, quoted, JSON-wrapped and ambiguous answers. Same parse in any other workflow that reads a sha from an agent (`wave-review.js`, `sdd-wave.js`).

**Tier:** ordinary (`.claude/workflows/**`). Own PR, CI only.

followUps.title: Request short reference uses the UUIDv7 timestamp prefix, identical for requests within ~65 s
followUps.body:
`shortReference` in `packages/web-ui/src/panel/RequestList.tsx:73` is `reference.slice(0, 8)` of a UUIDv7 correlation id. The first 8 hex characters of a UUIDv7 are the high bits of the millisecond timestamp, so every request made within about 65 seconds gets the same short reference (BW3 full e2e: 755 log lines share `01a139c3`).

**Effect:** the Copy action, the screen reader announcement and placeholder rows name requests ambiguously. In a busy shift a dispatcher cannot tell two recent requests apart by their short reference.

**Fix:** take the short form from the random part (for example the last 8 hex characters), keep the full id where it is shown in full, and update tests and e2e that match the old prefix. Check `apps/web` for other `slice(0, 8)` uses of the correlation id.

**Tier:** ordinary (`packages/web-ui`, `apps/web`). Own PR, CI only.

followUps.title: fixture-policy: non-Latin decimal digits (Arabic-Indic, Devanagari) slip the digit-run and freeText checks
followUps.body:
Minor from the #638 fix review (`fix/m2-gate-minors`, artifact `docs/reviews/fix-m2-gate-minors.md`, 10-14-26).

`packages/core/src/config/fixture-policy.ts:154`: NFKC folds full-width digits but not other Unicode decimal digits (Arabic-Indic U+0660-0669, Devanagari U+0966-096F, and so on). The run check treats them as non-alphanumeric separators and strips them, so a `status` or `serial` made of nine such digits passes. The freeText check (`/\d/` at :181) has the same ASCII-only gap.

**Fix:** use Unicode classes (`\p{Nd}` for digits, `\p{L}` for letters) with the `u` flag in the run and freeText checks; RED-first cases for Arabic-Indic and Devanagari digit runs; the shipped mock still passes.

Not realistic for the mock, but the policy is the guard that keeps fixtures from looking like real records (CLAUDE.md, spec 5.4, 10.8).

**Tier:** gate (`fixture-policy.ts`). Ride the next gate-tier PR.

Refs #638.

followUps.title: WS parser drops a known message type with an unknown enum value (a lost resync means no refetch)
followUps.body:
Found in the M2 demo minors PR (`fix/m2-demo-minors`, #66 work, 10-14-26).

The WS message parser tolerates unknown message types and unknown fields (ADR-0013, tested), but it **drops a known message type that carries an unknown enum value**: the tests assert that a message with `status: "notAStatus"` is dropped. When a later milestone adds a value to an existing enum (for example a new `resync.reason` or `sourceStatus.status`), an older client silently discards the whole message. A dropped `resync` means the client never refetches, so the request list goes stale with no sign.

**Decision needed:** keep dropping (and require that enum additions bump the protocol), or accept the message with the unknown value mapped to a safe fallback (for `resync`: refetch anyway; for a status: show a neutral "unknown" state). Record it as an ADR-0013 amendment.

**Tier:** critical (`packages/core/src/contracts/ws.ts`, `ws-events.schema.json`); contracts are frozen outside a contract wave, so this rides M2 P0-W3 with #622 or the next contract touch. Opus high review.

Refs #66, #622.

followUps.title: Key rotation for DATA_KEY and CREDENTIAL_KEY: ruling and ADR (M3 planning)
followUps.body:
**Goal (developer, 10-16-26):** the module ends up with full key rotation for both `DATA_KEY` and `CREDENTIAL_KEY`. The ruling and an ADR are made in the M3 planning session; M3 P1 (encrypted credential storage) is the recommended home, so both keys share one rotation design and one critical review.

**Where it stands**
- M2 P0-W3 (#524) rules option A: `request_key.key_version` records the wrapping `DATA_KEY` version (`REQUEST_KEY_VERSION = CURRENT_KEY_VERSION`, `packages/api/src/keys/request-keys.ts`), bound into the wrap AAD. That is the prerequisite for rotation; no rotation procedure exists.
- Spec v2 section 2 lists "credential key rotation (a `key_version` column is recorded, no rotation procedure is built)" as a non-goal. `DATA_KEY` rotation is not designed. `SECURITY.md` states both.

**For the ADR to decide**
- Rotation procedure for each key: re-wrap job (`request_key` rows; `state_credential` rows from M3 P1), batching, resumability, and what happens to rows written mid-rotation.
- Coexisting key versions during a rotation: how the old and new keys are supplied (Docker secrets), canaries for each version, fail-closed boot rules, and when the old key may be removed.
- Whether a separate row format version is needed (option B from #524) or the key version stays the only version.
- Audit events for a rotation (who, when, key, versions, row counts), and the runbook in `docs/deploy.md`.
- Backups taken under the old key: retention window (spec 8.6) and restore after rotation.
- Amending the spec non-goal; updating `SECURITY.md` built and planned lines.

Refs #524, #511, #311.

- [ ] m4: the non-query early-return chain in `AuditEventSchema` (`audit.ts:583-597`) has 13 clauses. A positive check of the query types would be shorter and fail safe on new types.
- [ ] Auth audit hardening: cover `passwordChanged` together with `loginSucceeded` so a failed audit write cannot leave a changed password with a live session and no row (double-failure residual, ruled "stands for P0" in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-05-m2-p0-contracts.md` Rulings; SEC-010).

followUps.title: Decision: hard REST refusal (403) for bearer requests with a foreign Origin?
followUps.body:
**Context (M2 P2 CW2, #723, 10-18-26).** A REST request with a bearer token and a foreign Origin gets no CORS grant and no preflight grant, but the server does not refuse it: Better Auth's origin check runs only for cookie sessions. The WebSocket upgrade does refuse a foreign Origin with 403. The manager accepted this reading for P2 (ruling on #723), and the developer asked to decide it properly later.

**Options**
- **A (current):** keep it as is. The Origin checks guard ambient cookie credentials (review c061), and a browser never sends a bearer token on its own, so a foreign page cannot use a victim's token.
- **B:** refuse with 403 any REST request whose Origin header is present and foreign, bearer or cookie. Defense in depth and one rule everywhere. Cost: a gate-tier change in `packages/api/src/http/security.ts` and `auth/**`, plus tests; it may block a future native or host integration that sends an Origin.

**Recommendation:** A for now, and revisit with the M4 host integration (CAD host embedding), where the real callers and their Origins are known.

Decide before M2 exit, or move to M4 P1.

followUps.title: Sweeper minors: tick counts on select failure and start() during stop() (C-M1, C-M2)
followUps.body:
Follow-up from the AW1 critical wave-review (`docs/reviews/feat-m2-a-p3-wave-1.md`, approve at f5c0cc0). Both items were rated Minor: no audit or data risk, no production path today. Critical tier (`packages/api/src/dispatch/**`).

- [ ] **C-M1** `packages/api/src/dispatch/sweeper.ts` (`expireSessions`, lines 74-80): a select failure on batch 2 to 4 rejects `tick()` after earlier sessions committed, so the tick's counts are lost and its prune is skipped. Committed sessions keep their `sessionRevoked` rows and the next tick prunes, so nothing is lost. Fix: catch a later batch's select failure inside `expireSessions`, log the error class only (spec 5.9), stop selecting, and return the counts so the prune still runs. Test first.
- [ ] **C-M2** `sweeper.ts` lines 162-166: `start()` called while a `stop()` is still pending clears the halt flag, so the in-flight tick resumes its remaining batches. `startup.ts` cannot reach this (start once; stop on listen failure, drain and fatal close). Fix: refuse `start()` while a stop is pending, or document the sweeper as not restartable. Test first.
- [ ] **Stale comment** `sweeper.ts:153`: the `fire()` catch says the session select failed and "nothing changed". With multiple batches, earlier sessions may have committed. Reword it with the C-M1 fix.

IDs: SEC-010, NFR-003; spec 5.2, 8.1. Refs #760, #786.

followUps.title: CW3 review follow-ups: ADR-0015 and deploy.md lock wording (first), db-reset wrapper catch, PUBLIC_ORIGIN tests, EAI_AGAIN

Follow-ups from the CW3 wave-review (`feat/m2-c-p3-wave-3`, artifact `docs/reviews/feat-m2-c-p3-wave-3.md`, approve at 4184a54, 10-20-26; critical slice Opus 5.5 `high`, gate slice Opus 5.5 `medium`). All minor; the PR scope was frozen. Ruling (M2 Manager 10, 10-20-26): one issue, and **C-m1 is the first fix**, because a doc that overstates a safety guard is worse than a missing one.

- [ ] **C-m1 (first fix)** `docs/decisions/0015-demo-database-reset.md:28` and `docs/deploy.md:104`: both say the write lock is taken "before deleting anything" or "first", and that every refusal "leaves nothing behind". In the code (`packages/api/src/ops/db-reset.ts:111-117`), the lock is a point-in-time busy check, released before the backup and the unlink (ruling 1); the HTTP probe is the primary guard. A refusal after the open can also follow loadDeps' normal start writes. Reword both docs to match. ADR-0015 is accepted, so a wording correction follows the ADR README rule for accepted ADRs, or a superseding note.
- [ ] **G-m1** ADR-0015 says the only secrets printed are "the seed's own one-time passwords"; `add-demo-users` accounts print too (`db-reset.ts:228`). Name both.
- [ ] **G-m2** `scripts/ops/db-reset.ts:26-27`: `readDeployEnv` and any non-`Refused` throw from `runDbReset` escape as an unhandled top-level rejection (a stack trace, exit 1). No secret leaks, but the output shape differs from the documented refusals. Wrap the call and print `db-reset: <name>` through `errorFields`, then exit 1.
- [ ] **G-m3** `packages/api/test/env.test.ts:83-92`: the exact-origin cases cover `CORS_ORIGINS` only. `PUBLIC_ORIGIN` got the same tightening (`env.ts:86`) with no case of its own, and the default-port refusal (`https://a.example.test:443`) is untested. Add a `PUBLIC_ORIGIN` case and a `:443` case.
- [ ] **Note (critical slice; allowed by ruling 1):** `EAI_AGAIN` counts as "stopped" (`db-reset.ts:56`), so a transient DNS failure while the app runs passes the probe; the write-lock check is then the only guard. Decide whether `EAI_AGAIN` should be "unknown" (refuse). Related: a rerun within the same second reuses the backup directory (`mkdirSync` recursive).

followUps.title: Demo database: seed, wipe and reseed at will (db:reset)
followUps.body:
The demo needs to be seeded, and wiped and reseeded, at will. Today `seed.js` runs only on an empty database, and `docs/demo.md` says there is no reset "by ruling".

Developer 10-20-26: nice to have before the M2 exit (after the must-have: promote on a seeded deploy through `config:import`, AW2 Task 7).

## Design (manager proposal, accepted by the developer 10-20-26)

- [ ] Ops command `db:reset` (`packages/api/src/ops/db-reset.ts`, wrapper `scripts/ops/db-reset.ts`): stop or refuse while the app runs, take a backup through the existing backup path first, delete the database, run migrations and the seed, then `add-demo-users`; the app starts after.
- [ ] Refuses unless the mock gate is on (demo on mock data only) and `--confirm <site>` names the site.
- [ ] Never prints anything secret except the seed's own one-time password output; the developer runs it on the host, never a session.
- [ ] ADR: a demo-only exception to "audit rows are never deleted" (SEC-010 to SEC-013): a reset deletes the whole database after a backup, so the history stays recoverable from that backup. It supersedes the "no reset" ruling in `docs/demo.md`.
- [ ] Docs: `docs/deploy.md` and `docs/demo.md` (reset and reseed steps).
- [ ] Tier critical (`db/**`, seed, audit): critical `wave-review` at Opus 5.5 high.

Owner: Lane C, wave CW3, its own PR, after CW2.

followUps.title: CI: tie the e2e shard total to the matrix (strategy.job-total) (#748 G-m1)
followUps.body:
**From:** the #748 gate wave-review (`docs/reviews/ci-m2-p3-shard-image.md`), residual minor G-m1. Ruled a follow-up by M2 Manager 10 on 10-20-26.

**Problem.** In `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, the `e2e` job runs `playwright test --shard="$SHARD/3"`. The total `3` is written separately from `strategy.matrix.shard: [1, 2, 3]`. Each value has its own assertion in `scripts/ci/ci-workflow.test.ts`, but nothing ties the two together. If someone shrinks the matrix and forgets the total (for example, the matrix becomes `[1, 2]`), a third of the suite is skipped and CI still passes. It fails open.

**Fix (gate tier, `.github/**` and `scripts/ci/**`).**
- Pass `TOTAL: ${{ strategy.job-total }}` through env next to `SHARD`, and run `--shard="$SHARD/$TOTAL"`.
- Add a test asserting the run uses `$TOTAL`, the env reads `strategy.job-total`, and the matrix list is `1..n` with no gaps.
- This can ride the next gate wave PR (CLAUDE.md "Split small fixes by tier").

Refs #748
